_comment: Keys that start with an underscore are notes, not jobs. Each job below is an invented example; replace them with your own. window_hours is the span that miss rate, queue delta and item counts are computed over. tier is native (the job calls record itself) or wrapped (pow-run.py records it from outside). Each invariant is its kind, that kind's parameters, and a why sentence saying what red means.

nightly-backup.description: Copies the documents folder to a second disk every night.

invariants.why: Red means the backup has not even started in over a day: the schedule is gone or the machine was off.
Red means no run has copied anything in over a day, even if runs keep exiting 0. A backup that reports success while copying nothing is the failure this catches.
Red means the last three runs in a row copied nothing or failed, a pattern that one good run earlier in the week could otherwise hide.

inbox-sync.description: Pulls new messages into the local mailbox every 15 minutes and reports how many are still waiting.

invariants.why: Red means more than one in ten of the runs that tried to sync failed. A day with nothing to pull is fine, but only when the job itself said there was nothing.
Red means the waiting backlog grew by more than 5 messages across the day, so the job is falling behind even if every run looks fine.
Red means not a single message was synced in the whole day, which for a busy mailbox means the sync is connected to nothing.

weekly-report.description: Builds a summary report every Monday morning and writes it to a shared folder.

invariants.why: Red means no report has been produced in over a week: this week's report is missing.
Red means more than a quarter of all runs this week could not build the report, counting quiet runs too.
